question: Which people call God “Olódùmarè”?
fact: Olódùmarè is the Almighty. The Yoruba also say Ọlọ́run, “Owner of heaven”. Their full Bible, Bíbélì Mímọ́, was completed in 1884 under Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther.

question: Which people call God “Chukwu” or “Chineke”?
fact: Chukwu is chi + ukwu, “the Great Spirit”. Chineke is “the Spirit who creates”. The CMS Niger Mission landed at Onitsha in July 1857.

question: Which people call God “Ubangiji”?
fact: Ubangiji means “Lord” or “Master”. The first complete Hausa Bible was published in 1932, from Walter Miller’s work in Zaria.

question: Which people call God “Abasi”?
fact: The Ibibio and Annang also call God Abasi; Abasi Ibom means “God the Great”. The Efik Bible is N̄wed Abasi, “the Book of God”, completed in 1868.

question: Which people call God “Osanobua”?
fact: Portuguese missionaries reached Benin in 1515 under Oba Esigie. Holy Aruosa Cathedral, from around 1517, is one of the oldest churches in Nigeria.

question: Which people call God “Aôndo”?
fact: Aôndo is also the Tiv word for the sky. Missionaries arrived at Sai on 17 April 1911, and the full Tiv Bible, Bibilo, was presented in 1964.

question: Which people call God “Oghene”?
fact: You can hear it in names like Oghenetega and Oghenekaro.

question: Which people call God “Tamuno”?
fact: Tamuno is used in the eastern Niger Delta: Kalabari, Okrika, Nembe and Bonny.

question: Which people call God “Ọjọ”?
fact: The Igala Bible is Ọtakada Ọla Ọjọ, “the Book of God’s Word”, published in full in 1970.

question: Which people call God “Oritse”?
fact: You can hear it in names like Oritsetimeyin. In the 1570s Olu Atorongboye was baptised Sebastião, the first Christian Olu of Warri.

question: Their full Bible (1884) was led by a translator who had been freed from a slave ship as a boy.
fact: Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther was rescued from a slave ship in 1822 and became the first African Anglican bishop. The Yoruba call God Ọlọ́run, “Owner of heaven”.

question: Missionaries landed at Onitsha in July 1857 to bring the gospel to them.
fact: The CMS Niger Mission was led by Crowther and J.C. Taylor. Archdeacon T.J. Dennis finished the Union Igbo Bible in 1913. The Igbo call God Chineke, “the Spirit who creates”.

question: A Church of Scotland mission reached Calabar in 1846, and Mary Slessor later served among them.
fact: Hope Waddell’s mission landed on 10 April 1846. The Efik call God Abasi, and their Bible is N̄wed Abasi, “the Book of God”.

question: Holy Aruosa, one of the oldest churches in Nigeria, was founded in their capital around 1517.
fact: It was founded in Benin City in the time of Oba Esigie. The Edo call God Osanobua.

question: Their state is called the “Food Basket of the Nation”, and missionaries reached Sai in 1911.
fact: The Dutch Reformed mission there grew into the NKST church. The Tiv call God Aôndo, the same word as “sky”.

question: At Easter 1867, the chiefs of Bonny publicly renounced the monitor-lizard juju.
fact: Bonny is an Ijaw kingdom in the Niger Delta. Ijaw Christians in the east call God Tamuno.

question: A 16th-century king of theirs became a Christian, and his son studied in Lisbon and Coimbra.
fact: Olu Atorongboye was baptised Sebastião, and his son Dom Domingos studied in Portugal. The Itsekiri call God Oritse.

question: Their king, the Attah, reigns at Idah.
fact: Idah sits on the River Niger in Kogi State. The Igala call God Ọjọ, and their Bible is Ọtakada Ọla Ọjọ.

question: Their first complete Bible (1932) came out of Zaria, and their alphabet has the letters ɓ, ɗ and ƙ.
fact: Walter Miller of the CMS worked on it in Zaria. Hausa Christians call God Ubangiji, “Lord”.

question: Ughelli and Sapele, in Delta State, are their towns.
fact: The Urhobo call God Oghene, as in the names Oghenetega and Oghenekaro.
